pairs.registryProposal: waiver-names-its-finding is written for change-review gates. Data-write guards with an operator override flag (--supersede, --allow-unstamped) are a common second home for blanket waivers, and the technique could name that case: the override should carry the conflicting stored ref or ids it accepts.

pairs.evidence: eslint-rules/README.md:34 The context's README promises that a drifted shim fails the tests, but the runner that checks these shims turns MODULE_NOT_FOUND on any shim into 'SKIP shim equivalence' with exit 0. techniques.evidence: packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/__tests__/run-all.mjs:116 A could-not-run is folded into a passing run. Deleting one shim drops the whole equivalence check, including shims already compared.

packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/__tests__/run-all.mjs:115 The standalone condition is read from the error the violation produces, not derived from whether eslint-rules/ exists. In-repo, the only way to get no data is the drift itself, so SKIP is the wrong resolution.
packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/__tests__/run-all.mjs:111 When it runs, equivalence is checked on the resolved module object, not on shim text.
eslint-rules/README.md:21 States that lint never loads these shims, so a green lint says nothing about them and only the rule-suite runner owns that question.

pairs.registryProposal: unmeasurable-criteria's 'derive the unmeasurable state; do not merely read a flag' could name the self-inflicted case: when the error used to detect 'context absent' is the same error the violation raises, the skip predicate must be derived from the container (does the directory exist) or the gate fails open on exactly the defect it guards.
